emitters.name: Saudi Aramco
emitters.description: State-controlled integrated oil supermajor; largest single producer of crude in the world (~9 Mbbl/d).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Upstream operations are unusually carbon-efficient per barrel (low water cut, associated-gas capture). Scope 3 dominates because customers combust the ~13M bpd of hydrocarbons sold.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero Scope 1+2 by 2050 for wholly-owned operations; expanding CCS at Jubail hub.

emitters.name: ExxonMobil
emitters.description: Largest US-listed integrated oil & gas company; upstream + refining + petrochemicals + Low Carbon Solutions unit.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Scope 1 comes from flaring, process heaters and refining. Guyana and Permian growth increases absolute emissions even as intensity/barrel falls.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero Scope 1+2 in operated assets by 2050; $20B Low Carbon Solutions capex through 2027 (CCS, hydrogen, lithium).

emitters.name: Shell plc
emitters.description: European integrated major; largest global LNG trader; retail fuel + renewables + trading.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Refining and gas processing dominate Scope 1. Scope 3 from customer combustion ~20× Scope 1+2 — typical for downstream-heavy majors.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; 50% Scope 1+2 reduction by 2030 vs 2016; softened Scope 3 intensity targets in 2024.

emitters.name: Chevron
emitters.description: US integrated major; Permian, Kazakhstan (TCO), Australia LNG (Gorgon), refining on US west coast.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Gorgon LNG's CCS project is one of the world's largest but has underperformed. Permian growth pushes absolute Scope 1 up despite methane-reduction programs.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero upstream Scope 1+2 by 2050; $10B low-carbon capex through 2028 (renewable fuels, hydrogen, CCUS).

emitters.name: TotalEnergies
emitters.description: French integrated major diversifying into electricity and renewables (Integrated Power segment ~20 GW gross capacity).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Refining + LNG processing drive Scope 1. Faster renewables ramp than US peers slows Scope 2 growth.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050 together with society; -40% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2015; 100 TWh renewable generation by 2030.

emitters.name: BP plc
emitters.description: UK integrated major; retail fuel, aviation, EV charging (bp pulse), biofuels, offshore wind JV.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: 2023 revision walked back 2030 oil-and-gas production cut from -40% to -25%, so Scope 3 trajectory flattens.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; revised 2030 emissions targets in Feb 2023 and again in 2024.

emitters.name: ConocoPhillips
emitters.description: Largest US pure-play E&P; no refining. Alaska Willow, Permian, Eagle Ford, LNG offtake.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Pure-upstream footprint: flaring + fugitive methane + drilling energy. Marathon acquisition (2024) increases absolute Scope 1.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero Scope 1+2 operated by 2050; -50% GHG intensity by 2030 vs 2016; zero routine flaring by 2025.

emitters.name: Marathon Petroleum
emitters.description: Largest US independent refiner; 13 refineries, 3.0 Mbbl/d capacity; Speedway divested to 7-Eleven.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Refining process heat is inherently CO2-intensive; renewable diesel projects (Martinez) shift feedstock mix but not absolute Scope 1 much.
emitters.climateCommitments: -30% Scope 1+2 GHG intensity by 2030 vs 2014; methane intensity -75%.

emitters.name: Phillips 66
emitters.description: Refining + midstream + chemicals JV with Chevron (CPChem); Rodeo renewable-fuels conversion.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Rodeo (California) conversion from crude refining to renewable diesel reduces future Scope 1 intensity per barrel.
emitters.climateCommitments: -30% Scope 1+2 emissions intensity by 2030 vs 2019.

emitters.name: Valero Energy
emitters.description: Largest independent refiner globally by throughput; second-largest US corn-ethanol producer via Diamond Green JV.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Renewable diesel capacity (~1.2 Bgy) reduces lifecycle emissions of sold fuels but does not shrink refinery-side Scope 1.
emitters.climateCommitments: -63% displacement of GHG emissions from products by 2035 (includes renewable fuels).

emitters.name: Duke Energy
emitters.description: Regulated electric + gas utility for ~8.2M customers across Carolinas, Florida, Midwest.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Still ~26% coal in generation mix (down from 61% in 2005). Coal retirements + gas + solar + nuclear rebalance is driving Scope 1 down ~5%/yr.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero electricity by 2050; -50% Scope 1 by 2030 vs 2005; full coal exit by 2035.

emitters.name: Southern Company
emitters.description: Regulated utility for the US Southeast; owns Georgia Power, Alabama Power. Operator of Vogtle 3 & 4 (first new US reactors in 30+ years).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Vogtle 3 (2023) + Vogtle 4 (2024) come online → step-down in fossil generation share. Coal retirement pace slower than northern US utilities.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; -50% GHG by 2030 vs 2007 (already achieved 49%).

emitters.name: NextEra Energy
emitters.description: Parent of Florida Power & Light (regulated) + NextEra Energy Resources (largest US wind/solar developer, ~35 GW).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Emissions per MWh already among the lowest of major US utilities; further declines depend on FPL gas fleet retirements.
emitters.climateCommitments: Real Zero by 2045 — zero Scope 1+2+3 without offsets; interim -70% CO2 by 2025 vs 2005.

emitters.name: American Electric Power
emitters.description: One of the largest US transmission owners; serves 5.6M customers across 11 states.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Coal share ~41% in 2023, planned to fall below 25% by 2030 as ~5 GW coal retires.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2045; -80% Scope 1 by 2030 vs 2005.

emitters.name: ENGIE
emitters.description: French multi-utility; gas networks + power gen (large renewables + remaining coal exit by 2027).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Rapid coal retirement (last plant closes 2027) and renewables build (+4 GW/yr) drive steepest Scope 1 decline in European utilities.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero across scopes by 2045; -45% Scope 1+2+3 by 2030 vs 2017.

emitters.name: United Airlines
emitters.description: Global network carrier; largest transpacific US operator; SAF and next-gen fuel investor (Alder, Cemvita).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Jet fuel combustion is ~98% of footprint; fleet renewal (787, A321neo, MAX 10) improves fuel/ASM by ~1-2%/yr.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050 without traditional offsets; 3 Bgy SAF equity investments; direct-air-capture partnership (1PointFive).

emitters.name: Delta Air Lines
emitters.description: US legacy carrier with the industry's most premium-mix revenue; refinery ownership (Trainer, PA).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Owns its own refinery (rare) — Trainer emissions consolidated in Scope 1. Retired MD-88/90 fleet accelerated efficiency gains.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; -45% jet fuel by 2035 via SAF, fleet, ops.

emitters.name: American Airlines
emitters.description: Largest US airline by fleet size; hubs at DFW, CLT, MIA, PHX.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Standard fleet-driven emissions; SBTi-validated 1.5C-aligned intensity target.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; SBTi -45% CO2/RTK by 2035 vs 2019.

emitters.name: Southwest Airlines
emitters.description: US low-cost carrier; all-737 fleet; short/medium-haul point-to-point.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Single-fleet + shorter stage lengths → lower absolute footprint than legacy peers, but slightly worse per-ASM than long-haul-heavy carriers.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; 10% SAF blend by 2030.

emitters.name: International Airlines Group
emitters.description: Parent of British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Vueling, LEVEL.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Falls under UK-ETS + EU-ETS + CORSIA — one of few airline groups already paying an explicit carbon price on part of emissions.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; 10% SAF by 2030 (industry-leading commitment).

emitters.name: A.P. Moller-Maersk
emitters.description: World's second-largest container liner; first shipping major to order methanol dual-fuel vessels at scale (~24 on order).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Bunker fuel oil (HFO/VLSFO) is ~99% of Scope 1. Methanol vessels only marginally shift 2024–25 numbers.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2040 across the business — the most aggressive shipping target of a major liner.

emitters.name: FedEx
emitters.description: Global express + freight logistics; owns one of world's largest cargo airline fleets (FedEx Express).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: ~60% of Scope 1 is aviation jet fuel; ground fleet electrification (BrightDrop, Ford E-Transit) reduces ground share only.
emitters.climateCommitments: Carbon-neutral operations by 2040; $2B invested in vehicle electrification, SAF, DAC.

emitters.name: United Parcel Service
emitters.description: Global package delivery + supply chain; smaller aviation share than FedEx (UPS Airlines still top-10 US cargo carrier).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Rolling Laboratory alt-fuel fleet + ORION routing shaves per-package emissions ~1%/yr.
emitters.climateCommitments: Carbon-neutral by 2050; 30% SAF in air by 2035.

emitters.name: Union Pacific
emitters.description: Largest US Class-I railroad; 32,000-mile network west of Mississippi.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Diesel locomotives dominate Scope 1. Rail is already ~4× more fuel-efficient per ton-mile than trucking.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; -26% locomotive intensity by 2030 vs 2018 (SBTi 1.5C).

emitters.name: ArcelorMittal
emitters.description: World's second-largest steelmaker outside China; ~60 Mt crude steel per year across 15+ countries.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Blast-furnace (BF-BOF) route emits ~1.8 t CO2 / t steel — the single highest-emission industrial process at scale. DRI-EAF conversion (Sestao, Hamburg) reduces per-ton intensity but requires green hydrogen.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; -25% CO2/t globally by 2030; XCarb portfolio (recycled + reduced + hydrogen DRI).

emitters.name: Nucor
emitters.description: Largest US steelmaker; 100% electric-arc-furnace (EAF) — recycles scrap rather than smelting iron ore.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: EAF route emits ~0.4 t CO2/t steel — ~4× less than BF-BOF. Scope 2 dominates because of grid-electricity draw at mini-mills.
emitters.climateCommitments: -35% Scope 1+2 intensity by 2030 vs 2015; procuring 24/7 clean power (Duke, TVA).

emitters.name: Cleveland-Cliffs
emitters.description: Largest US flat-rolled steel producer; vertically integrated from iron ore mining to finished products.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Integrated BF-BOF footprint. Hydrogen trials at Middletown Works targeting 2030+.
emitters.climateCommitments: -25% Scope 1+2 GHG by 2030 vs 2017.

emitters.name: BHP Group
emitters.description: World's largest mining company by market cap; iron ore, copper, coking coal, nickel, potash.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Scope 3 dwarfs Scope 1+2 because customers (steelmakers, coal-power utilities) combust/smelt the products.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero operational (Scope 1+2) by 2050; -30% by 2030 vs 2020.

emitters.name: Rio Tinto
emitters.description: Global diversified miner; iron ore (Pilbara), aluminium (world's largest), copper, minerals.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Aluminium smelting is electricity-intensive → most Scope 2 sits in Canadian hydro-powered smelters (low intensity) vs Australian coal-grid alumina refining (high intensity).
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050; -50% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2018; ELYSIS inert-anode smelting JV with Alcoa/Apple.

emitters.name: Holcim
emitters.description: World's largest cement producer outside China; leader in supplementary cementitious materials (SCM) and calcined clay.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Cement chemistry (limestone calcination) releases ~50% of process CO2 before any fuel is burned — inherently hard to abate without CCS.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2050 (SBTi 1.5C validated); ECOPlanet low-carbon cement range.

emitters.name: CRH plc
emitters.description: Largest building-materials company in North America post-NYSE move; cement + aggregates + roads.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Cement kilns dominate Scope 1; aggregate/asphalt segment much lower intensity.
emitters.climateCommitments: -30% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2021; net-zero by 2050.

emitters.name: Dow Inc.
emitters.description: Largest US-listed materials-science company; plastics, industrial intermediates, performance materials.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Steam-cracker furnaces (ethylene) drive Scope 1; Path2Zero Fort Saskatchewan project targets first net-zero-emissions integrated cracker (electric + CCS, ~2027 start-up).
emitters.climateCommitments: -30% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2005; carbon-neutral by 2050.

emitters.name: LyondellBasell
emitters.description: Global chemicals and polymers producer; olefins, polyolefins, refining (Houston to shut down 2025).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Houston refinery shutdown (2025) removes ~5 Mt/yr Scope 1. Circular polymers segment scaling via MoReTec pyrolysis.
emitters.climateCommitments: -42% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2020; net-zero by 2050.

emitters.name: BASF
emitters.description: Largest chemical company in the world by revenue; integrated Verbund production at Ludwigshafen.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Steam crackers + ammonia synthesis + power plant at Ludwigshafen dominate. Green-hydrogen ammonia and electric-heated crackers in pilot.
emitters.climateCommitments: -25% Scope 1+2 by 2030 vs 2018; net-zero by 2050.

emitters.name: Toyota Motor
emitters.description: World's largest automaker by volume (~10M vehicles/yr); hybrid pioneer, slower BEV ramp than peers.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Scope 3 (use-phase of sold vehicles) is >90% of total — typical for automakers. Hybrid-heavy mix keeps sold-fleet CO2/km lower than most peers.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero vehicles by 2050; -33% Scope 3 CO2/vehicle by 2035 vs 2019.

emitters.name: Ford Motor
emitters.description: US Big-3 automaker; F-Series #1 US vehicle; Model e (BEV) + Ford Pro (commercial) restructured 2023.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Manufacturing Scope 1+2 modest; the dominant number is Scope 3 tailpipe from ~4M ICE vehicles sold/yr.
emitters.climateCommitments: Carbon neutrality by 2050; SBTi-validated 1.5C alignment.

emitters.name: Tesla
emitters.description: Largest pure-BEV automaker + energy storage + solar; vertically integrated cell + vehicle manufacturing.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Manufacturing Scope 1+2 comparable to a mid-size industrial; the interesting number is *avoided* emissions (~20 Mt CO2 in 2023 per Tesla Impact Report) from displacing ICE miles.
emitters.climateCommitments: Master Plan 3 = full electrification of economy; own manufacturing net-zero target undated.

emitters.name: Walmart
emitters.description: Largest company in the world by revenue; 10,500+ stores; largest US private employer.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Scope 2 (store + DC electricity) dominates own footprint. Project Gigaton engages ~5,900 suppliers to cut Scope 3.
emitters.climateCommitments: Zero emissions across operations by 2040 (no offsets); Project Gigaton avoided ~750 Mt CO2e since 2017.

emitters.name: Amazon
emitters.description: Global e-commerce + AWS cloud + advertising + logistics (own airline Prime Air, delivery fleet).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Owned logistics (aviation, trucking, last-mile van fleet) drives most Scope 1 — Amazon's footprint looks more like a logistics carrier than a retailer.
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero by 2040 (The Climate Pledge); 100% renewable electricity matched (achieved 2023).

emitters.name: Microsoft
emitters.description: Software + Azure cloud; datacenter energy demand growing rapidly (AI training + inference).
emitters.emissionsNarrative: AI datacenter build-out pushed 2023 emissions +29% vs 2020 baseline — a public reversal that shows how hard even 'low-carbon' businesses are to decarbonize under growth.
emitters.climateCommitments: Carbon negative by 2030; remove all historical emissions since 1975 by 2050.

emitters.name: Alphabet (Google)
emitters.description: Global search + advertising + YouTube + Google Cloud + Waymo.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Datacenter power draw + supplier manufacturing (Scope 3) drives most of the footprint. 2023 emissions +48% vs 2019 baseline (AI build-out).
emitters.climateCommitments: Net-zero across operations & value chain by 2030; 24/7 carbon-free energy by 2030.

emitters.name: Apple
emitters.description: Consumer electronics + services; corporate operations already carbon-neutral since 2020.
emitters.emissionsNarrative: Scope 2 reported as zero due to matched renewable procurement. Supplier manufacturing (Scope 3, especially aluminium + display + logic) is the real footprint.
emitters.climateCommitments: Carbon-neutral entire footprint by 2030 (Apple 2030); already carbon-neutral for corporate ops.
